sentences.text: The petitioners filed this petition U/Sec.166 of M.V.Act,1988 claiming compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- from respondents due to death of Neyaz Ahmad in a road traffic accident.

2. Brief facts of petitioners case are that, on 26-07- 2023 at about 11.00 a.m. the deceased Neyaz Ahmad was crossing the Queens Road, Opposite to Shifa Hospital, Shivajinagar, wherein the rider of the Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-04/KJ-0138 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering to human life, came at high speed from Queens & Thimmaiah Road Junction in a zigzag manner and dashed against the deceased and caused the accident.
Due to forced impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident,
the deceased was shifted to Shifa Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and further shifted to NIMHANS Hospital and again return back to Shifa Hospital, wherein admitted as an inpatient during the course of treatment he succumbed to the accidental injuries on 29-07-2023 at about 1.35 p.m. thereafter body was shifted to Bowring Hospital Mortuary, wherein Postmortem was conducted and after postmortem the body was shifted to to their native by using an Airways and Ambulance for which they have spent a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- and also performed funeral,
obsequies, last rites ceremony for which petitioners have spent more than Rs.3,00,000/-.

sentences.text: Prior to the date of accident deceased was hale, healthy and aged about 38 years and working Mason Work at Shifa Hospital, Bangalore and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. he was only earning member in the family and to look after his family.

The petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased and she has lost the loving and caring husband at her early age and the petitioner No.2 to 4 are children of the deceased who have lost the caring father and the petitioners were depending upon the deceased morally and financially.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the family members are completely broken and facing financial difficulties.

4. The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA- 04/KJ-0138, against whom the Shivajinagar Traffic Police have registered criminal case in Cr.No.47/2023 for the offences punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is being RC owner and Respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners prays to grant the compensation.
5. In pursuance to the notice, Respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal and hence he was placed as Ex-parte.
Respondent No.2 has appeared through its Counsel and filed Written statement.
6. Brief averments of the written statement of Respondent No.2 are that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the same is liable to be dismissed in limine.

It is contended that the driver of the insured vehicle/respondent No.1 i.e., insured cum rider was not having valid and effective D.L. to drive the said vehicle as on the date of the alleged accident and as such respondent No.1 has willfully violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
There was no negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle as he was proceeding with due care and cautious by following the traffic rules and regulations.

On the contrary the alleged accident occurred due to sole negligence of the deceased who was crossing the road in a negligent manner without following the traffic rules and regulations, by colluding with the police, a false complaint was foisted against the insured vehicle in order to get compensation illegally and high handedly, as such this respondent specifically denied the contents of the police documents.

Further, denied the age,
income and occupation of the deceased and denied the relationship of deceased with the petitioners.
It is contended that, the compensation amount claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated, arbitrary and speculative.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

sentences.text: The Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation aimed at providing relief to the victims or their families, in cases of genuine claims.
In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of Filial Consortium.
Parental consortium is awarded to children who lose their parents in motor vehicle accidents under the Act.
A few High courts have awarded compensation on this count.
However, there was no clarity with respect to the principles on which compensation could be awarded on loss of Filial Consortium.
The amount of compensation to be awarded as consortium will be governed by the Principles of awarding compensation under "Loss of consortium" as laid down in Pranay Sethi (Supra).
In the present case, we deem it appropriate to award the father and the sister of the deceased, an amount of Rs.40,000/- each, for loss of Filial Consortium.
Hence, the Petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for compensation amount at Rs.40,000/-each under the head Loss of Filial Consortium.

offending vehicle was duly insured at the time of accident, but rider of the said vehicle was not having valid D.L.

sentences.text: In view of the judgment of Apex Court in the case of Pappu (supra), as per the conditions of the policy, the insured vehicle must be driven by the driver of the vehicle, who is having effective driving licence.
In this case, it is not so.
Therefore, there is a violation of the policy conditions by the owner of the lorry.
As M.V. Act is a benevolent legislation, the claimants cannot be deprived of the compensation so awarded in this case.

Therefore, if the Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation, as the policy was in force as on the date of accident, as the Insurance Company has to indemnify the said compensation so awarded in view of the principle laid down in the aforesaid judgments by the Hon'ble Apex Court, it would meet the ends of justice.
However, the Insurance Company is at liberty to recover the same from the owner of the lorry by executing the award against him.
On perusal of the above said ratio, it is clear that even after fundamental breach, the insurer has liability to pay the third party/petitioners and recover the same from the owner.
